headline: Profit surges as margins widen and credit quality improves
summary_short: Citizens Financial Group reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $587M, up 35% y/y and 14% q/q, with diluted EPS of $1.30 (+41% y/y) as net interest margin rose to 3.17% and fee income grew 8% q/q on record Capital Markets and Wealth results.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 4.4% q/q and 14% y/y as NIM expanded to 3.17%, benefiting from swap-termination effects, Non-Core runoff, and fixed-rate asset repricing. Fee income increased 8% q/q to $652M, led by record Capital Markets ($153M) and Wealth ($102M) fees. Pre-provision profit rose 13% q/q to $889M with positive operating leverage of 4.1% q/q and 6.4% y/y. Credit quality improved: net charge-offs fell to 37bps (-2bps q/q) and nonaccrual loans declined 4% q/q, though the CET1 ratio slipped to 10.4% from 10.5%. Citizens repurchased $225M of shares and paid a $0.46/share dividend, ending the quarter with $26.2B of stockholders' equity and tangible book value per share up 1% q/q to $38.29.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to net interest income growth (higher NIM from swap terminations, Non-Core runoff and fixed-rate repricing) plus record Capital Markets and Wealth fees.
Growth reflects the revenue increase and a lower provision for credit losses ($134M vs $164M y/y), partially offset by higher noninterest expense from Private Bank hiring.
EPS growth outpaces net income growth due to a lower diluted share count (426.7M vs 436.5M a year ago) from continued buybacks.

Company attributes the rise in period-end borrowed funds primarily to an increase in FHLB advances, partially offset by declining auto-collateralized borrowings as that portfolio runs off.
Y/y growth reflects retained earnings accumulation; q/q was roughly flat as retained earnings growth was offset by $225M of buybacks and $197M of common dividends paid in the quarter.
CEO Van Saun calls it an "outstanding" quarter, citing strong revenue growth, positive operating leverage, and favorable credit performance, with confidence in momentum through 2027.
